 Judgment

Respondent No.2 - insurer in MVC No.260 of 2011 on the file of the learned District Judge and MACT, Gadag (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity), is impugning the judgment and award dated 28.01.2003, awarding compensation of Rs.5,29,350/- with interest at 6% per annum,
from the date of petition till its realisation and directing respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.
2. Parties are referred to as per their ranks and status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are that, the claimant claimed compensation for the injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.
It is contended that on 27.08.2011 at about 5.00 p.m., he was riding the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-26/L-1160 from Mulagund side towards Gadag.

In the meantime,
the tractor bearing registration No.KA-26/T-1025 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed the motor cycle, as a result of which, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 District Hospital, Gadag and thereafter to KIMS Hospital, Hubli, where he took treatment as inpatient by spending huge amount.
In spite of taking treatment, he suffered permanent disability.
Therefore, respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer are liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 remained exparte and has not contested the matter.
5. Respondent No.2 filed the objection statement denying the contention taken by the claimant.

It is contended that the tractor bearing registration No.KA-26/T-1025 was attached with trailer bearing registration No.KA-26/310, but the driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the tractor-trailer.
Thereby, he has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. On the basis of these pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 "1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in the road traffic accident by vehicle bearing its Reg.No.KA 26/TA 1025 and KA 26/L 1160 on 27.08.2011 at 5.30 p.m. near Poultry Farm on Gadag-Mulagund road?

7. The claimant examined himself as PW1 and got examined PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P194 in support of his contention.
Respondent No.2 got examined RW2 and got marked Exs.R1 and 2 in support of its defence.

The Tribunal after taking into consideration all the materials on record,
answered issue Nos.1 and 2 in the Affirmative and awarded compensation of Rs.5,29,350/- with interest at 6% per annum and held respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally responsible to pay the compensation.
8. Being aggrieved by the same, the insurer is before this Court.
Heard Smt Preeti Shashank, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Chandrashekar P Patil, learned counsel for respondent No.1 and Sri S M Kalwad, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials including the Trial Court records.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the vehicle involved in the accident is the tractor attached with trailer.
The driver was holding the driving licence to drive only the tractor w.e.f. 16.07.2008.

Under such circumstances, it is to be held that the driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the tractor trailer and the insurer should be exonerated from paying compensation.
11. Learned counsel further submitted that the claimant has suffered only two fractures and was admitted as inpatient for about 19 days.

The Tribunal awarded exorbitant amount of Rs.96,000/-
under the head loss of future earning on account of permanent disability, without any basis.
No material are placed before the Tribunal to prove the income of the claimant.
Inspite of that, the Tribunal has taken the income of the injured at Rs.8,000/- per month without any basis.
The compensation NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 awarded under other heads are also without any basis.
Hence, she prays for allowing the appeal and to modify the impugned judgment and award.
12. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1- claimant opposing the appeal submitted that the driver was holding valid and effective driving licence.
Copy of driving licence produced as per Ex.R2 and it was valid on the date of accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal was right in rejecting the claim of the insurer.
He further submitted that the Tribunal has assigned valid reason to award compensation in favour of the claimant and there are no reason to interfere with the same.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

13. In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:

sentences.text:
My answer to the above point is in 'Partly in the Affirmative' for the following:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 REASONS 14.

The first contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is with regard to the validity of the driving licence of the driver who drove the tractor-trailer, which was involved in the accident.
Ex.R2 is the copy of driving licence of the driver who was driving the tractor-trailer on the date of accident.
As per Ex.R2, the driver was authorized to drive the tractor (NT) w.e.f. 16.07.2008.
The accident has occurred on 27.08.2011 i.e., during the validity of driving licence.
The only question that arises for consideration is as to whether the driving licence to drive the LMV (NT) is valid for driving the tractor attached with trailer.

15. This position is discussed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan Vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 1, after recording its earlier decision in Nagashetty Vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd., 2 and held in para 43 as under:
"43. Section 10(2) (a) to (j) lays down the classes of vehicles to be driven, not a specific kind of motor vehicles in that class.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Nagashetty Vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd., 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If a vehicle falls into any of the categories, a licence holder holding licence to drive the class of vehicle can drive all 2017 ACJ 2011 2001 ACJ 1441 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 vehicles of that particular class.
No separate endorsement is to be obtained nor provided, if the vehicle falls in any of the particular classes of section 10(2).

This Court has rightly observed in Nagashetty (supra) that in case submission to the contrary is accepted, then every time an owner of a private car, who has a licence to drive a light motor vehicle,
attaches a roof carrier to his car or a trailer to his car and carries goods therein
, the light motor vehicle would become a transport vehicle and the owner would be deemed to have no licence to drive that vehicle.
It would lead to absurd results.
Merely because a trailer is added either to a tractor or to a motor vehicle it by itself does not mean that driver ceased to have valid driving licence.

In our considered opinion, even if such a vehicle is treated as transport vehicle of the light motor vehicle class, legal position would not change and driver would still have a valid driving licence to drive transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class, whether it is a transport vehicle or a private car/tractor attached with trolley or used for carrying goods in the form of transport vehicle.

The ultimate conclusion in Nagashetty (supra) is correct,
however, for the reasons as explained by us."
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 Thus the position of law is made clear in the above decision.
Hence, the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted.
16. The second contention raised is with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

Ex.P170 is also the discharge note, according to which, claimant was once again admitted to the hospital on 25.11.2011 and was discharged on 30.11.2011.
Therefore, the claimant was treated as inpatient for a total period of 63 days.
. PW2 is the doctor who treated the claimant and deposed before the Court.
He has issued Ex.P193-the disability certificate, assessing the disability at 48% to the particular limb.
The Tribunal assessed it to the whole body at 10%, which is just and reasonable.
18. According to the claimant, he was working as driver and was also doing agricultural work.
In the absence of any material to support the income, the guidelines issued for reckoning the compensation before the Lok Adalath could be taken into consideration.
Since the accident is of the year 2011, the income of the claimant could be taken at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Therefore, the compensation towards loss of future earning could be assessed at Rs.1,08,000/- (6000 x 12 x 10% x 15).
The claimant has produced medical bills as per Exs.P7 to P182 amounting to Rs.2,12,350/-, for which he is entitled to.
19. Looking to the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment, the claimant is entitled for compensation towards conveyance, attendant ad other incidental charges at Rs.20,000/-.

He is also entitled for compensation towards loss of income during laid up period amounting to Rs.18,000/-,
for - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 future medical expenses Rs.10,000/- and towards loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-.

Since the claimant has suffered two fractures and underwent treatment for 63 days, he is also entitled for compensation towards pain and suffering at Rs.40,000/-.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,29,350/-, but he is entitled to the compensation at Rs.4,38,350/-.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7494 interference.

Hence, I answer the above point partly in affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 28.01.2003 passed in MVC No.260 of 2011 on the file of the learned District Judge and MACT, Gadag, is hereby modified.
(iii) It is held that the claimant is entitled to compensation at Rs.4,38,350/- with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.5,29,350/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the compensation is reduced by Rs.91,000/-.
The amount in deposit, if any, be transmitted to the Tribunal, forthwith.
Registry to draw the award accordingly and to send back the Trial Court records along with copy of the judgment and award.
